description:
If your final dir is a network share, you may wish to copy the file to a staging directory to then have a background thread copy to the network.

This allows me to keep be able to keep up speed. The build directory is a tmpfs, the stage directory is a local hard disk, and the final directory is a NFS share over 1 Gbe network. So it's rather slow.

I had to branch the code, to make other branches. So I'm resubmitting the pull request.

comments.body: `stage_dir` should be `tmp_dir` by default. otherwise it's like `directout` would be enabled by default.

I just did a k16 test with every combination. The -s option assumes -d is also set, I need to check if -s is set without -d also set and error out.

-t -2 -s -d
build in -t/-2, write final to -s, then copy to -d (intended function of the code).

-t -2 -d
build in -t/-2, write final to -d (default directout function)

-t -2 -s
build in -t/-2, write final to -s, then it copies to -t
This needs to error out.
Fixed the default to be tmp_dir.

Pondering more, just fixing the default to tmp_dir seems to resolve the odd -t -2 -s behavior.

By that I mean if they intended to stage_dir it in the -s directory and then copy back to tmp_dir, it does what they asked via the options. So working as intended?

Thanks
My only goal was that not specifying `stage_dir` results in the same behavior as if this code was never merged. And now it's the case yes.
This check needs to be above line `stage_dir = tmp_dir;`
Moved it above the assignment. Apologies for so many issues, it worked well in my testing. But I apparently didn't check for everything. I appreciate your reviews.
Found trailing / check also needed to be moved up.
